# nish/net/quic-recovery

QUIC loss detection and congestion control (RFC 9002): the packets each packet number space has in flight, the round-trip estimate, loss by packet and by time threshold, the probe timeout with its backoff, NewReno, and a pacer. Sans-IO: it never sees a byte of a packet, only packet numbers, sizes and the caller's clock.

```ts
import {
  QUIC_RECOVERY_APPLICATION,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_APPLICATION_CAPACITY,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_DATAGRAM_SIZE,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_DEFAULT_MAX_ACK_DELAY,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_CAPABLE,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_FAILED,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_TESTING,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_TESTING_PACKETS,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_UNKNOWN,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_ECT0,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_GRANULARITY,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_HANDSHAKE,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_HANDSHAKE_CAPACITY,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_INITIAL,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_INITIAL_RTT,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_INITIAL_WINDOW,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_MAX_BACKOFF,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_MINIMUM_WINDOW,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_PACKET_THRESHOLD,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_PERSISTENT_THRESHOLD,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_LOSS,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_NONE,
  QUIC_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_PTO,
  QuicRecovery,
  QuicSentPackets,
} from "nish/net/quic-recovery";
```

```ts
import { QuicRecovery, QUIC_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_PTO } from "nish/net/quic-recovery";

const recovery = new QuicRecovery();
const slot: i32 = recovery.onPacketSent(space, pn, size, now);     // every ack-eliciting packet
recovery.onAck(space, frame.ackRanges, frame.ackRangeCount, delay, now);
… recovery.spaces[space].acked / .lost name the slots it settled …
if (now >= recovery.deadline(blocked)) { recovery.onTimeout(now, blocked); }
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="Quic​Recovery" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#quicrecovery">

One connection's loss recovery and congestion control, across its three packet number spaces.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Quic​Sent​Packets" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#quicsentpackets">

The ack-eliciting packets one space sent, in a ring of `capacity` slots in the order they went out: slot `slot(k)` is the `k`-th from the oldest still kept, for `k` below `count`.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-detail title="What it tracks">

Each space keeps its ack-eliciting packets in a fixed
ring (`QuicSentPackets`), in the order they were sent, so the memory is
fixed when the connection is made and nothing is allocated per packet. A
packet that elicits no acknowledgement (one that carries only ACK, PADDING
or CONNECTION_CLOSE) is not recorded: it is never in flight, and neither
an RTT sample nor a loss is ever taken from it (RFC 9002 §2, §5.1). The
caller keeps what each packet carried in its own arrays, indexed by the
slot `onPacketSent` answers, and reads `acked` and `lost` after each
`onAck` and `onTimeout` to learn which slots were settled. A slot named
there keeps its packet number, time and size until the next call.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Time and units">

Every time and every duration is the caller's
monotonic clock in milliseconds, which is also the timer granularity
(`QUIC_RECOVERY_GRANULARITY`, §6.1.2), and the arithmetic is Appendix A's
and Appendix B's in integers: `smoothed_rtt = (7 × smoothed_rtt +
adjusted_rtt) / 8`, `rttvar = (3 × rttvar + |smoothed_rtt −
adjusted_rtt|) / 4`, each division truncating. Sizes are bytes.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The pacer's clock">

Pacing is not a timer, and on a path whose round
trip is under a millisecond a pacer that counts whole milliseconds earns
nothing until the next one starts, and then waits a whole one. So a
caller with a finer clock sets `micros` to the same instant in
microseconds before it calls in, and the pacer, its budget and its own
smoothed RTT (`pacerRtt`) count microseconds; loss detection and the
probe timeout still count milliseconds, at least
`QUIC_RECOVERY_GRANULARITY`. A `micros` outside the millisecond `now`
names, a stale one or none, is not read: the pacer counts `now × 1000`
then, and paces as a millisecond clock always did.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="What the server leaves out">

It is written for the server side of a
connection: there is no client anti-deadlock probe (§6.2.2.1), since a
server never has to send to unblock its peer. A congestion window that
the sender does not use is not grown (§7.8): an acknowledgement grows it
only if, when it arrived, the bytes in flight were at least half the
window.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="ECN">

**ECN** (§7.1, B.7; RFC 9000 §13.4.2 and its Appendix A.4). A caller that
marks its packets ECT(0) asks `ecnCodepoint()` what to mark with, says so
with `onEctSent` for every packet it marked, and hands an ACK_ECN frame's
counts to `onAckEcn`. The counts are validated against the packets marked
before they are used: an ACK that newly acknowledges a marked packet
without counts, a count that falls, counts past the packets marked, or an
increase in ECT(0) and ECN-CE short of the marked packets newly
acknowledged fails validation, as does every packet of the testing period
being lost, and a failed path is marked no more (`QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_FAILED`).
Only the first `QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_TESTING_PACKETS` are marked until one
validates. A rise in the ECN-CE count is a congestion event, from the
largest packet newly acknowledged, so it halves the window once per
recovery period as a loss does. Counts that arrive with an ACK that does
not raise the largest acknowledged are neither validated nor used: they
may be older than those already read.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="What a peer cannot do">

Every input is checked: the ranges of an
acknowledgement are read only up to the count given and the array's
length, a packet acknowledged twice counts once, and
the backoff stops doubling at `QUIC_RECOVERY_MAX_BACKOFF`, so no duration
overflows. A peer that never acknowledges anything costs a probe each
timeout, at a rate that halves each time, until the idle timeout ends the
connection.

</scalar-detail>

Written from RFC 9002 §5 to §7 and its Appendices A and B, in this
module's own structure; nothing here is ported from another
implementation. Private names carry the `quicRecovery` prefix
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e).

## Classes

### QuicRecovery

One connection's loss recovery and congestion control, across its three
packet number spaces. The fields are readable: the RTT estimate
(`latestRtt`, `smoothedRtt`, `rttVar`, `minRtt`), the window
(`congestionWindow`, `ssthresh`, `recoveryStart`), `ptoCount`, and the
counts a test or a log reads (`congestionEvents`, `persistentCongestions`).

```ts
class QuicRecovery
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new QuicRecovery()` | Makes the state a new connection has, as `reset` leaves it: every space empty, the RTT estimate and the window at their initial values. |
| `congestionEvents: i32` | How many congestion events reduced the window, and how many of them were persistent congestion. |
| `congestionWindow: i64` | congestion_window (B.2), in bytes. |
| `ecnCongestionEvents: i32` | How many congestion events a rise in the ECN-CE count caused (§7.1). |
| `ecnState: i32` | ECN's state, `QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_TESTING` until a marked packet's counts validate or fail. |
| `ecnTestLost: i32` | How many marked packets were lost before ECN validated: once it reaches `ecnTestRecorded`, ECN fails (RFC 9000 A.4). |
| `ecnTestRecorded: i32` | How many of the packets marked while testing ECN are recorded in a space's ring, so their loss can be seen. |
| `ecnTestSent: i32` | The packets marked while testing, and of those recorded, how many and how many of them were lost. |
| `firstSampleTime: i64` | When the first RTT sample was taken, or -1 before it: persistent congestion counts only packets sent since (§7.6.2). |
| `handshakeConfirmed: boolean` | Whether the handshake is confirmed (RFC 9001 §4.1.2), which the caller sets: the peer's max_ack_delay then bounds its ACK delays, and the Application Data space has a probe timeout. |
| `latestRtt: i64` | latest_rtt (§5.1): the last sample, in milliseconds. |
| `maxAckDelay: i64` | The peer's max_ack_delay in milliseconds (RFC 9000 §18.2), which the caller sets once it has read it. |
| `micros: i64` | The caller's clock in microseconds, which it sets before each call when it keeps one, or -1. |
| `minRtt: i64` | min_rtt (§5.2): 0 until the first sample. |
| `pacerBudget: i64` | The pacer's credit in bytes (§7.7), and the time it was last topped up in microseconds, or -1. |
| `pacerRtt: i64` | The smoothed RTT the pacer's rate is taken from, in microseconds: `smoothedRtt` on the pacer's clock. |
| `pacerTime: i64` | When the pacer's credit was last topped up, in microseconds on the pacer's clock, or -1 before the first time. |
| `persistentCongestions: i32` | How many of `congestionEvents` were persistent congestion (§7.6), which collapses the window to its minimum. |
| `ptoCount: i32` | pto_count (A.3): how many probe timeouts fired since the last acknowledgement. |
| `recoveryStart: i64` | congestion_recovery_start_time (B.2), or -1 outside recovery. |
| `rttVar: i64` | rttvar (§5.3): kInitialRtt / 2 until the first sample. |
| `smoothedRtt: i64` | smoothed_rtt (§5.3): kInitialRtt until the first sample. |
| `spaces: QuicSentPackets[]` | The sent-packet ring of each packet number space, indexed by `QUIC_RECOVERY_INITIAL` and its siblings. |
| `ssthresh: i64` | ssthresh (B.2): unbounded (2^62 − 1) until the first congestion event. |
| `timeoutSpace: i32` | The space the last `onTimeout` acted on, or -1. |
| `bytesInFlight(): i64` | bytes_in_flight (B.2): every space's packets in flight. |
| `canSend(): boolean` | Whether the window has room for another full-sized datagram (B.4). The caller sends nothing ack-eliciting while it has not, except a probe. |
| `deadline(amplificationBlocked: boolean): i64` | SetLossDetectionTimer (A.8): when `onTimeout` is next due — the earliest time-threshold loss, else the probe timeout — or -1 for none. With `amplificationBlocked`, when the server may send nothing until the client does (RFC 9000 §8.1), there is no probe timeout (§6.2.2.1). |
| `discardSpace(space: i32): void` | OnPacketNumberSpaceDiscarded (A.11): the space's keys are gone, so its packets leave flight uncounted, its timers stop, and the backoff resets. |
| `ecnCodepoint(): i32` | The ECN codepoint to mark the next packet with (RFC 9000 A.4): ECT(0) for the first `QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_TESTING_PACKETS` and, once the path is capable, for every one; 0, Not-ECT, while the testing packets wait to be validated and once validation failed. |
| `evictOldest(space: i32): i32` | Gives up the oldest packet still in flight in space `space`, taking it out of flight without a congestion event, so that a probe can be recorded when the ring is full. The caller has already queued what the space had in flight again, which is what a probe sends. Answers the slot, or -1 when nothing is in flight there. |
| `fineNow(now: i64): i64` | `now` on the pacer's clock: `micros` when it falls inside the millisecond `now` names, and `now × 1000` otherwise. |
| `lossDelay(): i64` | The loss delay (§6.1.2): 9/8 of the larger of the latest and the smoothed RTT, at least the granularity. |
| `onAck(space: i32, ranges: i64[], count: i32, ackDelay: i64, now: i64): i32` | An ACK frame for space `space` (A.7): `ranges` holds `count` `[smallest, largest]` pairs, highest first, as `QuicFrame.ackRanges` does, and `ackDelay` is the peer's ACK Delay in milliseconds. The packets newly acknowledged are listed in the space's `acked`, those it shows lost in `lost`; an RTT sample is taken when the largest acknowledged is newly acknowledged (§5.1), the window grows or shrinks (B.5, B.8), and the probe backoff resets. Answers how many packets were newly acknowledged, or -1, changing nothing, when the space does not exist or there is no range. A packet number the space never sent is the caller's to refuse (RFC 9000 §13.1): only it knows the packets that elicit no acknowledgement, which are not recorded here. |
| `onAckEcn(space: i32, ranges: i64[], count: i32, ackDelay: i64, now: i64, ect0: i64, ect1: i64, ce: i64): i32` | `onAck` for an ACK frame that carries ECN counts, `ect0`, `ect1` and `ce` as ACK_ECN gives them (RFC 9000 §19.3.2), or -1 each for one that carries none. The counts are validated (RFC 9000 §13.4.2.1) and a rise in ECN-CE is a congestion event (§7.1, B.7) before loss is detected, as A.7 orders it. |
| `onEctSent(space: i32, slot: i32): void` | A packet of space `space` went out marked ECT(0): `slot` is the one `onPacketSent` answered for it, or -1 for a packet that elicits no acknowledgement and so was not recorded. Every packet of a datagram marked counts, whatever `ecnCodepoint()` answers by the last of them. |
| `onPaced(now: i64, size: i32): void` | Charges the pacer for a datagram of `size` bytes sent at `now`. |
| `onPacketSent(space: i32, pn: i64, size: i32, now: i64): i32` | Records an ack-eliciting packet (A.5): number `pn` of space `space`, `size` bytes on the wire, sent at `now`. Answers its slot, under which the caller keeps what it carried, or -1, recording nothing, for a space that does not exist, a size that is not positive, a packet number that is not above the last one recorded, or a ring that is full. |
| `onTimeout(now: i64, amplificationBlocked: boolean): i32` | OnLossDetectionTimeout (A.9), at `now`. When a time-threshold loss is due, the space's packets are checked again and the lost ones listed in its `lost`: `QUIC_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_LOSS`. Otherwise, when the probe timeout is due, the backoff doubles and the caller is to send a probe in `timeoutSpace`: `QUIC_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_PTO`. Before either is due, or when nothing is timed, `QUIC_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_NONE`. |
| `pacerDelay(now: i64, size: i32): i64` | How many milliseconds after `now` the pacer lets a datagram of `size` bytes go: 0 when it may go now, else its wait in microseconds rounded up to whole milliseconds, so at least 1. The rate is 5/4 of the window per `pacerRtt` (§7.7's N of 1.25). |
| `pacerQuantum(least: i32, most: i32): i32` | The credit a paced flight waits for before it starts, in bytes: what the pacer earns in a millisecond, at least `least` and at most `most`. A pacer that earns by the microsecond would otherwise let a fast connection out a datagram at a time, one send each; one that earns slowly still lets a datagram go as soon as it has the credit for it. |
| `probeTimeout(): i64` | The probe timeout's period without backoff (§6.2.1): smoothed_rtt + max(4 × rttvar, kGranularity), plus the peer's max_ack_delay once the handshake is confirmed. It is also what a key update's old keys are kept for and what the idle timeout is at least three of. |
| `ptoTime(): i64` | GetPtoTimeAndSpace (A.8): when the probe timeout fires, the earliest over the spaces with an ack-eliciting packet in flight, with the backoff applied; the Application Data space counts only once the handshake is confirmed. Answers -1 with nothing in flight. |
| `reset(): void` | Puts everything back as a new connection has it: every space empty, the RTT estimate and the window at their initial values. A connection slot reused for another peer calls it; the rings are kept. |
| `space(space: i32): QuicSentPackets \| null` | Space `space`'s packets, or `null` for an index that names no space. |

### QuicSentPackets

The ack-eliciting packets one space sent, in a ring of `capacity` slots
in the order they went out: slot `slot(k)` is the `k`-th from the oldest
still kept, for `k` below `count`. A packet stays in its slot after it is
acknowledged or lost until every older one is settled too, which is what
lets persistent congestion see that nothing between two lost packets was
acknowledged (§7.6.2).

```ts
class QuicSentPackets
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new QuicSentPackets(capacity: i32)` | An empty ring; `QuicRecovery` makes one for each space. |
| `acked: i32[]` | The slots the last `onAck` acknowledged, `ackedCount` of them, oldest first. |
| `bytesInFlight: i64` | The bytes of this space's packets in flight. |
| `ce: i64` | The ECN-CE count of the last ACK_ECN frame validated in this space; a rise is a congestion event. |
| `count: i32` | How many packets the ring keeps, in flight and settled; a test reads it to see what a flight recorded. |
| `ect0: i64` | The ECN counts of the last ACK_ECN frame validated in this space (RFC 9000 §19.3.2). |
| `ect1: i64` | The ECT(1) count of the last ACK_ECN frame validated in this space. |
| `ectSent: i64` | How many of this space's packets, recorded or not, were sent marked ECT(0). |
| `fineSent: i64[]` | When each packet was sent on the pacer's clock, in microseconds. |
| `inFlight: i32` | How many recorded packets are still in flight: neither acknowledged nor lost. |
| `largestAcked: i64` | The largest packet number the peer acknowledged in this space, or -1. |
| `lastAckEliciting: i64` | time_of_last_ack_eliciting_packet (A.3), or -1 before the first. |
| `lastPn: i64` | The packet number of the last packet recorded, or -1: each must be larger (RFC 9000 §12.3). |
| `lossTime: i64` | loss_time (A.3): when the oldest packet not yet lost by the packet threshold becomes lost by time, or -1. |
| `lost: i32[]` | The slots the last `onAck` or `onTimeout` declared lost, `lostCount` of them, oldest first. |
| `lostCount: i32` | How many slots of `lost` the last `onAck` or `onTimeout` filled. |
| `state: u8[]` | Each slot's state, with `QUIC_RECOVERY_MARKED` set if its packet was sent marked ECT(0). |
| `timeSent: i64[]` | When each slot's packet was sent, the `now` `onPacketSent` was given, in milliseconds; loss detection and RTT samples read it. |
| `ackedSlot(k: i32): i32` | The `k`-th slot the last call acknowledged, or -1. |
| `fineAt(s: i32): i64` | When the packet in slot `s` was sent on the pacer's clock, in microseconds, or -1. |
| `full(): boolean` | Whether every slot is taken, so nothing more can be recorded until a packet is settled. |
| `inFlightAt(s: i32): boolean` | Whether slot `s` holds a packet still in flight. |
| `lostSlot(k: i32): i32` | The `k`-th slot the last call declared lost, or -1. |
| `markedAt(s: i32): boolean` | Whether the packet in slot `s` was sent marked ECT(0). |
| `pnAt(s: i32): i64` | The packet number in slot `s`, or -1. |
| `sizeAt(s: i32): i32` | The size of the packet in slot `s`, or 0. |
| `stateAt(s: i32): i32` | The state of slot `s`, or free for a slot outside the ring. |
| `timeAt(s: i32): i64` | When the packet in slot `s` was sent, or -1. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="128" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECOVERY_APPLICATION_CAPACITY: i32`

How many packets the Application Data space keeps in flight: 128
full-sized datagrams is 150 KiB in flight, a 12 Mbit/s path at a 100 ms
round trip, against what the record costs every connection from the
start. When the ring is full the space sends nothing that would elicit an
acknowledgement until one arrives, as if the congestion window were full.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECOVERY_HANDSHAKE_CAPACITY: i32`

How many packets the Initial and the Handshake space each keep in flight.
A server's handshake flight is a few datagrams, and the anti-amplification
limit holds it to three times what the client sent until its address is
validated, so 16 leaves room for several probes on top.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECOVERY_MAX_BACKOFF: i32`

The most times the probe timeout doubles (§6.2.1). Sixteen doublings of
the longest probe timeout a peer can cause still fit an `i64`, and by then
the idle timeout has ended the connection.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

Validation failed: nothing is marked again for the connection's life, unless `restartEcn` tests a new path.

`QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_TESTING: i32`

ECN's states (RFC 9000 A.4): testing, marking the first packets; unknown, those sent and none validated yet; capable; and failed, for the connection's life.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_TESTING_PACKETS: i32`

How many packets are marked while ECN is tested, before a marked one is acknowledged (RFC 9000 A.4).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECOVERY_ECN_UNKNOWN: i32`

ECN is unknown: the testing packets are sent, none is validated yet, and nothing more is marked
until one is.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECOVERY_PERSISTENT_THRESHOLD: i64`

kPersistentCongestionThreshold (§7.6.1): lost packets spanning three probe timeouts collapse the window.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_LOSS: i32`
